findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume and snapshots are stored unencrypted with no KMS customer-managed key.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public IP and DNS name, exposing the database endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it in a private subnet layer.
The master username is the default/administrative name 'admin', which is a predictable target for credential-guessing attacks against the publicly reachable endpoint.
The master password is supplied via var.password and stored in Terraform state in plain text rather than being generated/managed in Secrets Manager, making the credential broadly readable.

The EC2 user_data embeds the database username and password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and by any process that can reach the instance metadata service.

No metadata_options block is defined, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; an SSRF in the PHP application would allow unauthenticated retrieval of the instance role credentials (which grant s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*).
The instance defines no root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume containing the plaintext DB credential file is stored unencrypted.

The instance role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", which is effectively administrative over storage, compute and database services and enables privilege escalation (e.g. ec2:RunInstances with iam:PassRole-adjacent abuse, reading any S3 bucket).
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on every protocol and port, providing a data-exfiltration and command-and-control channel.
Port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group, and combined with publicly_accessible = true the database trusts far more sources than the workload requires.
No parameter forcing TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport) is set and the application connects with mysqli_connect without SSL, so database traffic including credentials travels unencrypted.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so clients may connect to the database over unencrypted channels.
